sections.html: • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (needs updating, IUCN 2010)

Africa: Lower Congo River. Type locality: tributary of the Lobi River, south-west of Efulen, and Kribi River, South Cameroon; Abanga River, Ogowe.

The species is widespread within the Central Africa assessment region.
These catfish inhabit fast flowing waters and spend a lot of their time clinging to aquatic leaves. If you provide long stemmed plants, such as Vallisneria, you will see this habit.

To keep this species and other members of this African hillstream family you will have to provide a well oxygenated planted aquarium and keep up your water changes, as they are not as hardy as their South American equivalents.

Commonly known as 'African Whiptails', these catfish look at first glance superficially like South American whiptails such as Rineloricaria/Hemiloricaria. Dorsal spines (total): 0; anal spines: 0. Diagnosis: caudal peduncle relatively short, 3–4.2 times in SL and slender, length 8–16 times depth. Etymology: the specific name brevicauda means 'with short caudal'.
